content.value_statement: GraphQL teams need schemas that scale across products, teams, and clients. This skill guides architecture, federation, caching, security, and operational planning.
actual_capabilities: Designs federated GraphQL schemas and subgraph ownership models.
Plans schema-first development with interfaces, unions, custom scalars, and versioning.
Recommends DataLoader, batching, persisted queries, and caching strategies.
Defines authorization, rate limiting, query cost, and introspection controls.
Guides subscriptions, live queries, and event-driven GraphQL patterns.
Outlines testing, monitoring, schema registry, and governance workflows.
limitations: It provides guidance and plans, not direct implementation in your repository.
It needs project context to tailor schema, resolver, and infrastructure choices.
It does not replace production security testing or load testing.
It focuses on GraphQL systems, not unrelated API or frontend work.

use_cases.title: Plan a federated platform
use_cases.description: Create domain boundaries, subgraph ownership, gateway responsibilities, and governance rules for a multi-team GraphQL platform.

use_cases.title: Optimize a slow API
use_cases.description: Identify resolver bottlenecks, N+1 risks, caching layers, query limits, and monitoring needs for a busy GraphQL API.

use_cases.title: Harden production GraphQL
use_cases.description: Design authorization, rate limiting, query complexity controls, introspection policy, and validation practices for sensitive APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Review my schema plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GraphQL schema plan. Identify missing types, weak relationships, naming issues, and changes needed before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve resolver performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this GraphQL API design for N+1 queries, cache opportunities, batching needs, and monitoring gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design federation boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a federated GraphQL architecture for these teams, domains, data sources, client needs, and ownership constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Create production readiness plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production readiness plan for this GraphQL platform covering security, performance, observability, testing, and schema governance.

output_examples.input: Design federation for an e-commerce platform with catalog, cart, order, and customer teams.
output_examples.output: A domain ownership plan, subgraph boundary map, gateway strategy, schema governance process, and rollout checklist.

output_examples.input: Optimize a GraphQL API with slow product queries and repeated database calls.
output_examples.output: A performance review covering batching, DataLoader usage, cache placement, query complexity limits, and resolver monitoring.

output_examples.input: Prepare a public GraphQL API for production launch.
output_examples.output: A launch plan covering authorization, rate limits, persisted queries, introspection policy, error handling, and operational dashboards.

best_practices: Provide business domains, data sources, traffic expectations, and client needs before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for tradeoffs between federation, monolithic schemas, GraphQL Mesh, and database-first approaches.
Validate recommendations with tests, benchmarks, threat modeling, and operational review before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a complete production design without sharing constraints or data ownership.
Do not skip resolver performance review when schemas aggregate multiple services or databases.
Do not treat schema design as stable without versioning, deprecation, and governance plans.

faq.question: Can this skill design Apollo Federation systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Apollo Federation v2, subgraph boundaries, gateway design, and schema governance.

faq.question: Can it help reduce N+1 query problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends batching, DataLoader patterns, field selection, caching, and resolver tracing.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: It can suggest implementation plans, but it is mainly an architecture and review skill.

faq.question: Can it review GraphQL security?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers authorization, query cost limits, rate limiting, introspection policy, and input validation.

faq.question: Is it useful for REST to GraphQL migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan migration steps, compatibility concerns, gateway patterns, and service ownership.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Share domains, users, data sources, current API shape, traffic goals, security needs, and team ownership.
